Delhi's air pollution surged after Diwali, but did India's official air quality readings capture just how bad it really was?
According to an assessment by the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM), firecrackers accounted for 71.1% of Delhi's PM2.5 pollution between 1 am and 9 am on November 9, the morning after Diwali. Two nights before Diwali, their estimated contribution was just 5.6%.
